title: Zone
description: A geographic unit of the crisis world. The zone id is the canonical location key: entities, hazards, signals, and actions all reference zones by id. The zone table is the single place that holds rich geodata (names, coordinates). Zones form a directed graph through downstream_of; hazards propagate along its edges with a delay.

id.description: Unique kebab-case identifier. The canonical location reference used by every other object.

name.description: Local place name as spoken (Paiporta). Used in voice calls, alerts, and the dashboard.

municipality.description: Municipality the zone belongs to. Often equal to name when the zone is a whole town.

province.description: Province or region (Valencia). Gives agents administrative context for jurisdiction and escalation.

country.description: ISO country name (Spain). Relevant for scenario packs outside Spain.

population.description: Inhabitants of the zone. Redundant with the population entity total; keep both equal.

downstream_of.description: Zone ids whose hazards propagate into this zone. The edges of the hazard propagation graph. Scenario-agnostic: for a flood the edge means water flows here; for a wildfire it would mean wind carries fire here.

propagation_delay_min.description: Minutes for a hazard in an upstream zone to reach this zone. This is the warning window the system must exploit: acting inside this window is the whole point.

elevation.description: Coarse exposure indicator. low elevation means higher flood exposure and more people at risk in garages and ground floors.

centroid.description: Representative coordinates of the zone. Used for map rendering and as a fallback for rough distance computation. Not a substitute for the propagation graph: straight-line distance misleads in a crisis (the 2024 hazard reached Paiporta through 40 km of rambla, not 6 km of straight line).

geometry.description: Optional GeoJSON polygon of the zone boundary, for map rendering only.

notes.description: Free-text context injected into agent prompts. Terrain, known choke points, historical behavior.
